title: Latency-first autoscale handoff and soft-slice playbook (PRD wip)
content:
Summary:
This is a working PRD sketch for a latency-first autoscaling handoff and a complementary soft-slice tenancy pattern for Dedicated capacity. Goal is to give latency-sensitive tenants predictable tail latency while allowing opportunistic bursts and preserving pool-level efficiency. This doc focuses on the handoff logic (when and how to prewarm/allocate) and the runbook/constraints for soft-slices (fractional, low-friction compute allocations that can be scaled down gracefully).

Why (problem):
- Customers running real-time features (chat, search rerank, call transcription) are extremely sensitive to 95/99p tail latency.
- Traditional autoscalers that use throughput/queue depth signals often react too late for tail latency spikes.
- Over-provisioning to meet tail SLAs is expensive. We need a mechanism that prioritizes latency SLOs while allowing efficient sharing of GPUs across tenants.

Primary goals:
- Primary safety: maintain tenant 99p latency SLO (configurable per-tenant).
- Minimum cost delta vs current dedicated model (target: <10% additional infra cost for typical workload mixes).
- Low friction for tenant owners: soft-slices should not require long procurement cycles.
- Observable and debuggable: clear telemetry and traces for handoff events and soft-slice transitions.

Non-goals:
- This is NOT a replacement for Reserved capacity commitments for steady heavy throughput.
- Not targeting extreme batch/offline workloads (those can use lower-fidelity lanes).

Terminology (working):
- latency-first trigger: signal derived from online percentiles (e.g., 95p or 99p) of model response time, smoothing + spike detector.
- handoff: process to move traffic from shared/oversubscribed pool to warmed capacity or to a higher-fidelity lane.
- soft-slice: ephemeral fractional reservation on a GPU (slot/time-slice/kv-prewarm budget) that provides better isolation than pure best-effort but is not a full reserve.
- fidelity-lanes: variants of model serving (full model, quantized small model, model-shim) used for guided degradation.

High-level design:
1) Signals and triggers (what we monitor):
   - P99 request latency per tenant route (primary).
   - Short-term latency spike detector (EWMA + jump detection window 30s).
   - KV cache hit-rate and per-tenant KV pressure (to detect cold-starts).
   - Pending queue length and evicted requests count.
   - GPU warmness metric: number of live KV-cache frames for tenant/model on node(s).
   - Model variant availability and compat flags.

2) Handoff policy (latency-first):
   - Normal: tenant served on shared pool with opportunistic scheduling.
   - Soft-trigger: if p95 > threshold for X seconds OR spike detector fires, create a soft-slice allocation (small fractional allocation) and prewarm KV cache + load model weights if needed.
   - Hard-trigger: if p99 > stricter threshold for Y seconds OR queue length above cap -> escalate to full reserved slot (if tenant has entitlement / credits) or route to fallback model variant and notify tenant.
   - Hysteresis: once handoff occurs, require stable good latency for K minutes before tearing down slice to avoid flapping.

3) Soft-slice semantics and controls:
   - Soft-slice is a lightweight reservation that guarantees: a small CPU/GPU slice (e.g., 10-25% of a slot) for a tenant's highest-priority requests, and a guaranteed minimum KV cache capacity (configurable).
   - Default soft-slice lifetime: 15 minutes (extendable while signals persist).
   - Eviction order: least-priority soft-slices -> opportunistic slices -> background batch. Soft-slices can be preempted for higher SLA tenants.
   - Billing: soft-slices are metered (per-minute) and billed at a premium multiplier vs shared (preview pricing idea).

4) Soft-slice placement and packing:
   - Placement advisor chooses nodes with highest existing warmness for tenant/model to minimize prewarm cost.
   - Follow bin-packing heuristic to co-locate compatible soft-slices (low KV overlap) to reduce memory blowup.
   - If no warm node available, consider cross-zone warm proxy (warm on different zone and route with slightly higher latency) as a temporary mitigation.

5) Graceful degradation and foldbacks:
   - Fallback lane: model-variant with slightly lower compute cost (e.g., 8-bit quantized, shorter decode length) activated as stepdown when escalating failure.
   - Progressive rollback: if soft-slice cannot be provisioned fast enough, route a fraction of traffic to fallback lane and throttle low-priority requests.
   - Alerting: create tenant-level alert when fallback used > 5% of requests in a 5m window.

6) Admission and fairness controls:
   - Soft-slices by default subject to pool-level maximum concurrency (to prevent headroom erosion).
   - Priority classification: SLA tiers (gold/silver/bronze) map to admission and preemption policies.
   - Burst credit account: tenants accumulate burst credits (time-weighted) used to request soft-slices beyond baseline. Credits decay and are visible in Console.

Telemetry and observability:
- Required dashboards:
  - Tenant latency heatmap (p50/p95/p99 over time) with handoff annotation markers.
  - Soft-slice inventory: active slices, node placement, warmness delta pre/post handoff.
  - Prewarm cost estimator: tokens used, GPU seconds, prewarm vs steady-state CPU/GPU usage.
- Traces and logs: every handoff produces a trace with trigger signal, matched ticket id (if created), list of prewarm ops and timings (model load, warm KV synced, slice bound).
- Alerts: automated alerts for ops: high prewarm churn (>N per hour), repeated flapping, pool headroom below X%.

Operator runbook (ops-friendly steps):
- Play 1 (tenant complains about 99p latency):
  1. Check tenant latency chart and handoff traces.
  2. If soft-slice was created: inspect node warmness and prewarm success; if prewarm failed, check model artifact health and network pulls.
  3. If no handoff occurred and p99 is high, consider increasing soft-slice eligibility or temporarily bump tenant priority.
- Play 2 (pool headroom drained):
  1. Identify top tenants consuming soft-slices and check credits/priority.
  2. Throttle low-priority soft-slices; consider temporary global soft-slice suspend.
  3. Communicate via status page if user-facing SLOs affected.

Rollout plan (staged):
- Stage 0: internal experiment in staging; collect signals and tune thresholds. (owner: Marco)
- Stage 1: opt-in beta for a few enterprise tenants with known workloads. Monitor cost/latency and iterate. (owner: Sofia)
- Stage 2: enable soft-slices across subset of pools with conservative admission caps. Add billing/console displays. (owner: Aisha)
- Stage 3: general availability with documented SLAs and pricing.

Mini experiments to run (metrics we care about):
- Experiment A: Latency-first trigger vs queue-depth-trigger for same tenant traffic. Metric: % time p99 > target during workload ramp; cost delta per hour.
- Experiment B: Soft-slice packing heuristics (co-locate vs spread): Metric: average prewarm GPU seconds per handoff, and memory pressure events.
- Experiment C: Fallback lane effect on perceived latency & quality (A/B with human eval set).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Frequent prewarm churn increases overall cost.
  Mitigation: enforce per-tenant rate limits for soft-slice creation and implement warmness scoring so prewarm only when likely to persist.
- Risk: Fragmentation of GPU memory leading to OOM.
  Mitigation: strict bins for KV cache reservation, conservative memory accounting, and hard OOM guard rails that evict opportunistic background jobs first.
- Risk: Billing confusion for customers.
  Mitigation: clear console UX, pre-warn tenants when soft-slice billing is about to be consumed, and allow opt-out.

Open questions (TODOs):
- Granularity: should soft-slice be time-sliced (fast context switch) or slot-fraction (reserved fractional CUDA resources)? Leaning toward slot-fraction as it's easier with current runtime, but needs kernel-level support.
- Prewarm latency: what is realistic end-to-end prewarm for large models (7B+) with current provisioning? Need quantified numbers (we have partial telemetry in staging).
- Billing model: per-minute billing vs credit consumption. Need finance input for price elasticity.
- UI: how to surface soft-slice usage and credits in Console without overloading customers? (Sofia to prototype).

Next steps / action items:
- Instrument p95/p99 spike detector in staging for a set of tenant routes (Devon).
- Run prewarm cost microbenchmarks for the 3 most common model families (Marco).
- UX sketch for Console showing credits and active soft-slices (Sofia).
- Draft proposal for billing model and speak to finance (Aisha -> finance meeting queued).
- Confluence page with runbook + escalation matrix (link placeholder: CONFCLOUD-5592).

Notes to self / rough ideas (brainstormy):
- Could we offer an "on-call fastlane" where customers can pay for instant soft-slice for an hour? Might map well to burst credits sold as bundles.
- Maybe keep a micro-warm pool per region with pinned tiny slices for top N enterprise tenants so handoff is near-instant. Cost vs benefit to measure.
- Look at tail-latency mitigation research: predict spike earlier using short-term rate-of-change of p50/p95. Might let us prewarm before p95 jumps.

Stakeholders and owners:
- Product owner: Aisha Patel (product-dedicated)
- Engineering lead (autoscale & runtime): Marco Li (eng-serving-runtime)
- Observability/telemetry: Devon Brooks (observability)
- UX/Console: Sofia Martinez (developer-experience)

Appendix: example trigger thresholds (initial suggestion, tunable):
- Soft-trigger: p95 > 200ms for 45s OR p95 change > 2x over 30s.
- Hard-trigger: p99 > 500ms for 30s OR queue length > 50 for 60s.
- Hysteresis: require p95 < threshold * 0.8 for 10 minutes before teardown.

Linked references and experiments:
- Draft autoscaler impl PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale/pull/478
- Staging telemetry dashboard (placeholder): CONSOLE-DASH:dedicated-autoscale-staging
- Relevant Jira epic: DEDICATED-312

End of draft.

-- aisha
